operations.evidence: The valid category list was tied to the requested year-month data-set edition.
Category validity was not assumed stable across months and metadata was not treated as a crime count.
Machine URL identifiers and human-readable category names were preserved as separate fields.
Display names were not used as stable join keys and categories were not treated as spatial evidence.
The availability endpoint's year-month list for street-level crime editions was recorded.
Availability was not represented as field completeness or parcel evidence.
Month-specific force identifiers supplying stop-and-search data were recorded.
A force absent from the monthly list was not converted to a zero count.
The force-list endpoint's explicit exclusion of British Transport Police was recorded.
BTP absence from this list was not generalized to every Police.uk endpoint.
Unique force identifiers and their reuse in force-specific requests were recorded.
Force identifiers were kept separate from neighbourhood identifiers and completeness claims.
Specific-force ID, URL and optional descriptive or contact metadata were recorded.
Contact metadata was not used as crime evidence and optional fields remained nullable.
Force-scoped neighbourhood identifier and name pairs were recorded.
Neighbourhood lists were not represented as parcel polygons.
The non-global, force-specific scope of neighbourhood identifiers was recorded.
Force and team identifiers were required together for unambiguous keys.
Latitude-longitude lookup returning force and force-specific neighbourhood identifiers was recorded.
The lookup was not represented as a cadastral or exact parcel join.
The documented caveat that a neighbourhood centre point may not be exactly central was recorded.
The locator point was not treated as a boundary centroid or parcel coordinate.
Associated neighbourhood locations, including possible police stations, were recorded as nested metadata.
Associated locations were not treated as incident locations and empty lists remained valid.
Optional address, postcode, telephone, type, coordinates and description fields were recorded.
Missing contact fields were not converted to negative evidence.
Neighbourhood-priority issue text and the date the priority was agreed were kept separate.
Narrative priority text was not converted into an incident rate.
Priority action text and the date action was last taken were kept separate.
Missing action text was not interpreted as proof of no police activity.
ISO start and end date-times plus event title, address and type were recorded.
Scheduled dates were not treated as proof that an event occurred.
Optional event contact metadata was recorded separately from description and address.
Absent contact details were not used as an event-status signal.
The standard JSON service contract and supported HTTP GET and POST transports were recorded.
Transport success was not treated as semantic completeness.
Neighbourhood teams, events, street crime, outcomes and nearest-station resource scope was recorded.
Resources with different update cycles were not collapsed into one metric.
The latest-month default and the possibility of no data for a selected force were recorded.
An empty latest response was not converted to zero and reproducible requests require a pinned month.
Rows 411-430 were checked against prior source identifiers and retained only as new endpoint-contract roles.
The H-to-F portable-root mismatch, stale PID 27880, non-current heartbeat and seven absent runtime outputs were rechecked; no runner or business task was started.
